# RustFS

Plugin ID `rustfs`. Buckets and capacity of a RustFS object store.

A panel on the Storage page shows the buckets of a RustFS object store and its capacity, read from
the store's series through the prometheus plugin. A bucket at 80% of its quota is a warning on the
Overview and at 90% critical; a bucket without a quota raises nothing. It is the one plugin that
is off until `plugins.rustfs.enabled` is `true`: nothing in its settings says an object store
exists.

## What it shows

### Pages

No page of its own.

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Storage (`storage`) | Object storage | `object-storage` |

### Contributions

It contributes attention items.

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `rustfs.usage` | `RustFSUsageData` | The object store's buckets with their usage and quota, and its capacity. |

## Dependencies

A change to a plugin's settings restarts it and the plugins that require or use it.

- **Requires** [Prometheus-compatible](prometheus.md): while it does not run or is `unavailable`, this plugin is `blocked` and its pages are hidden.

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.rustfs` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginsrustfs), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.rustfs.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.rustfs.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, ssh, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.bucketUsed` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_BUCKET_USED` | string | `rustfs_bucket_usage_usage_bytes` | no | no | Series of a bucket's used bytes, labelled bucket. The default is rustfs_bucket_usage_usage_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.bucketQuota` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_BUCKET_QUOTA` | string | `rustfs_bucket_usage_quota_bytes` | no | no | Series of a bucket's quota in bytes, labelled bucket. A bucket without one has no quota. The default is rustfs_bucket_usage_quota_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.capacityUsed` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_CAPACITY_USED` | string | `rustfs_cluster_capacity_used_bytes` | no | no | Series of the cluster's used bytes. The default is rustfs_cluster_capacity_used_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.capacityUsable` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_CAPACITY_USABLE` | string | `rustfs_cluster_capacity_usable_total_bytes` | no | no | Series of the cluster's usable bytes. The default is rustfs_cluster_capacity_usable_total_bytes. |

## Actions

None: the plugin only reads.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing.
